interactions.note: Web doesn't compute its area. It saves and restrains whichever creatures the caller names, wherever they are.
The engine turns the Cube to face any aim point, so a diagonal aim takes in 10 square centres.
The area, not the named list, decides who is hit. Both sides of the caster and creatures left off the list are tested.
The caster is outside her own Thunderwave. The creator's choice to include the origin has no hook.
The engine centres the Cube's height on the origin (±7.5 ft). Only readings that hold either way are tested: 5 ft up is in, 20 ft up is out.
Upcasting adds only damage, never size.
Total Cover from the origin is already tested under the cover units. Not repeated here.

The effect fixes the side length.

abuse.reason: A turned Cube takes in 10 square centres instead of 9.

abuse.reason: Web uses the caller's list and ignores its 20-ft Cube.

abuse.reason: The origin isn't included, and naming yourself doesn't aim the Cube.

not_testable.reason: The SRD puts the point of origin anywhere on a face. The engine always puts it at the centre of the face, so an off-centre placement can't be expressed: for example, a Thunderwave with the caster at one edge of the face, or at the bottom edge so the Cube rises 15 ft from the ground.
not_testable.infra_ticket: A way to place an area's point of origin off the centre of the Cube's face (sideways and vertically), through spells.cast and the Session cast command

not_testable.reason: 'unless its creator decides otherwise': the engine has no way for the creator to choose to include the point of origin (themself) in the area.
not_testable.infra_ticket: A choice hook on area spells to include the point of origin (the creator's own space) in a Cone or Cube

kind_waivers.reason: The point of origin is either included or not. There is no threshold to probe one step past.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.cube ambiguity 2: is a Cube on a grid aligned to the grid, or can it be turned freely, and is a creature in it when any part of its square is or only its centre?
rulings_proposed.ruling: A Cube is aligned to the grid and extends at right angles away from the face holding its origin. A creature is in it when the centre of its space is inside (as P-23). So a 15-ft Cube holds exactly 3×3 squares, a diagonal aim can't make it take in more, and the squares level with the origin's face (beside a Thunderwave caster) aren't in it.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.cube ambiguity 1: does 'the point of origin isn't included' leave out the creature whose space holds it (the caster of a Cube that originates from them)?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A, as P-25 for Cones: the creature at the point of origin isn't affected unless the creator chooses to include it, even if they name themself.

output.summary: I added 19 GLOSS.cube tests to tests/srd/test_glossary.py, using Thunderwave as the 15-ft Cube from Self and Web as the 20-ft Cube. The new tests ran with 17 passing and 2 failing because of the engine; the 2 are marked xfail and ruff is clean. The first red test: a diagonally aimed Cube is turned 45 degrees and takes in ten squares instead of 3×3. The second: Web doesn't compute its Cube at all and makes a named creature 100 ft away save against Restrained. The engine already gets right the direction, nothing behind the face, the side length (not a radius), the 20-ft height limit, no growth from upcasting or a far aim point, and the caster outside her own area. Two things are recorded as missing infrastructure: placing the origin off the centre of a face, and the creator's choice to include the origin. I proposed two rulings, grid-aligned Cubes with centre-of-space membership and the origin creature excluded (matching P-23 and P-25). I also added two new cheats to the abuse catalogue.
